decisions.quote: An exact replication of Vul et al. (2008) will be conducted as part of the Reproducibility Project. 12 participants (Note 5 required to achieve 95% power based on original findings) will be tested using the same hardware and similar software specifications used in the original study. Original code used to run the experiment and analyze results will be used. The key finding for replication is the reported three way interaction of SOA, measure, and target.
decisions.location: PRIMARY PROJECT REPORT 30 (https://osf.io/download/jupew/), Introduction, source_view.json line 409 (chunk_index 406)
decisions.reason: Primary Project Report 30 conducts a direct empirical replication of Vul, Nieuwenstein, & Kanwisher (2008) by collecting new experimental data from 12 participants at The University of Western Ontario using the attentional blink RSVP paradigm. Both shipped and blind correctly classify the study type as replication.

decisions.quote: Discussion Summary of Replication Attempt The analysis confirms the original effects observed by Vul and colleagues (2008), namely that selection is (a) suppressed (efficacy), (b) delayed (latency), and (c) diffused (precision) in time during the attentional blink as demonstrated significant main effects of each of these factors and by a significant three way interaction between SOA, measure (efficacy, latency, precision). The other main finding by Vul et al (2008) was that efficacy, latency and precision can be dissociated by their time course such that each effect returns to baseline at different SOA. These effects were also found as illustrated by comparing the figures from the original study with the replication results in Figures 1 and 2. While there are subtle differences in the specific results for the effects of suppression, delay and diffusion, the overall pattern of results is essentially the same between the original and replicated results. In sum the results from the original study by Vul et al (2008) were successfully replicated.
decisions.location: PRIMARY PROJECT REPORT 30 (https://osf.io/download/jupew/), Discussion - Summary of Replication Attempt, source_view.json line 417 (chunk_index 414)
decisions.reason: In Primary Project Report 30 (and CSV Study Num 117, where Replicate (R) = yes), all main effects of efficacy, latency, and precision as well as their focal three-way interaction with SOA and target were statistically significant (F(18, 660) = 12.98, p < .00001, compared to original F(18, 660) = 16.31, p < .00001), and the author explicitly concludes that the results from Vul, Nieuwenstein, & Kanwisher (2008) were successfully replicated.

decisions.quote: Discussion Summary of Replication Attempt Our results provide mixed evidence regarding the role of extremal edges defined by texture alone in depth perception. In our data, EE2 (a region with an extremal edge on the shared contour, and on the opposite contour) was chosen as closer than other textures, paralleling the original study. Likewise, when both regions had only one extremal edge, the one with the extremal edge on the shared contour was more likely to be perceived as closer (EE1>Convex1), though this effect was weaker than in the original study. However, we were unsuccessful in replicating the finding that EE1 regions are perceived as closer then Convex2 surfaces; this test asks whether an extremal edge on the shared contour is the dominant cue to depth in these stimuli, when pitted against the number of extremal edges (i.e. half cylinders are seen as close than quarter cylinders), and so constitutes a stringent test of the prediction. This final test was our a priori selected target of replication.
decisions.location: PRIMARY PROJECT REPORT 88 (https://osf.io/download/27cmh/), Discussion - Summary of Replication Attempt, source_view.json lines 952-953 (chunk_index 949-950)
decisions.reason: Although the project master table (Study Num 153) records Replicate (R) = no based solely on the single pre-selected key comparison EE1 > Convex2 (t(7) = 0.32, p = 0.76), the individual primary replication report for Palmer & Ghose (2008) tested all pairwise surface comparisons in its confirmatory analysis, replicated the significant depth-perception advantage for EE2 over Flat, EE1, and Convex1 as well as for EE1 > Convex1 (t(7) = 2.41, p = 0.04), failed to replicate EE1 > Convex2 and EE1 > Flat, and explicitly states in its Summary of Replication Attempt that the results provide 'mixed evidence' regarding extremal edges defined by texture alone in depth perception. Under the codebook, paper-level outcomes synthesize all tested comparisons for the original study and follow the authors' explicit overall mixed verdict.

decisions.quote: Discussion Summary of Replication Attempt The central goal of the current study was to investigate the replicability of the effects reported in Experiment 5 of Demany et al. (2008). We were able to replicate the significant main effect of ISI which showed that performance worsened as the interval between a chord and tone increased. Next, we also replicated the non-significant main effect of N, showing that N did not significantly affect performance. Finally, in contrast with the original study, we found that the effect of ISI on performance did not differ between chords with small or large N. Given that these data follow two of the three trends found by Demany et al. (2008), the current study qualifies as a partial replication. Commentary While this study qualifies only as a partial replication, we believe it is important to point out that the significant ISI x N interaction found in Experiment 5 was not anticipated given the prior trends and conclusions from Experiments 1, 2, and 4. Indeed, it was reported to only have occurred due to "unexpectedly high d' when N was equal to 1 and the ISI was 0 ms". Importantly, the central finding of Experiment 5 was replicated. Therefore, we believe our data to be mostly in line with the effects found by Demany et al. (2008).
decisions.location: PRIMARY PROJECT REPORT 59 (https://osf.io/download/wx74s/), Discussion - Summary of Replication Attempt and Commentary, source_view.json lines 679-680 (chunk_index 676-677)
decisions.reason: In Primary Project Report 59 (Demany, Trost, Serman, & Semal, 2008, Experiment 5), the Analysis Plan pre-specified three criteria for a successful replication: a significant main effect of ISI, a non-significant main effect of N, and a significant N x ISI interaction. While the project master table (Study Num 139) records Replicate (R) = yes for the single key main effect of ISI (F(3, 12) = 13.06, p < .001) and the Commentary notes that the central finding was replicated, the confirmatory ANOVA replicated two of the three pre-specified effects (significant main effect of ISI and non-significant main effect of N) but failed to replicate the significant N x ISI interaction (p > .05), leading the authors to explicitly conclude in both the Summary of Replication Attempt and Commentary that 'the current study qualifies as a partial replication' / 'qualifies only as a partial replication'. Under the codebook, an explicit author verdict of partial replication where some focal tested effects replicate and another does not maps to mixed.

decisions.quote: Replication of Study The Face of Success by Rule & Ambady (2008, Psychological Science) Casey Eggleston cm5hv@virginia.edu Minha Lee mhl5b@virginia.edu Thomas Talhelm tat8dc@virginia.edu Introduction Rule and Ambady (2008) found that naïve college undergraduates’ impressions of Fortune 500 CEOs’ appearance correlated with company profits. CEOs they rated as appearing more powerful and looking like good leaders ran companies with higher profits.
